{
  "entry_id": "abvigen_published_data_is_unreliable",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "Abvigen's published product data for the Red PS Fluorescent Particles-COOH line carries documented errors, including a monoclonal-antibody filing and the product name printed in the Particle Size field, in addition to excitation and emission figures that instrument testing has disproved. Nothing on that page should be treated as load-bearing without independent confirmation.",
  "identifiers": {
    "supplier": "Abvigen Inc",
    "catalogue_product": "AFR-0500-COOH"
  },
  "source": "prior_run:agentic-microscope@abvigen-verification-2026-09-06",
  "grade": "E3",
  "source_ref": "src_prior_abvigen_verification",
  "validity_conditions": "ABOUT A PUBLISHER, NOT ABOUT A BOTTLE, which is the whole reason this one crossed when the measurements beside it did not. 10.3 rule 1 caps a run taken elsewhere at E3 and, worse, a value about another laboratory's bottle needs a same-stock E5 assumption before it means anything here. This claim needs neither: it is about a document, and this store holds that document (src_abvigen_red_ps_cooh_datasheet), so it is checkable rather than inherited. THIS IS WHAT REVERSED TASK 015. The observation on this bench -- green-excited particles visible at 605 -- is equally consistent with `the bottle is not the Abvigen product` and with `the bottle is the Abvigen product and the sheet is wrong`, and a label that says nothing does not separate them either. What separates them is that the page is independently known to be careless, which makes the second explanation far cheaper. Kept as an entry rather than left in a commit message because a reversal whose reason is not on disk gets re-reversed by the next person holding the same data sheet. WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. It does not say every figure on the page is wrong, and it is not a licence to discard a published number because it is inconvenient. The seven entries taken from that sheet remain on disk at E3 about the type; two of them -- the excitation and emission peaks -- are marked disproved, and that marking rests on two independent instrument observations rather than on this entry. This entry lowers how much an unconfirmed figure from that supplier should be trusted; it does not by itself refute any particular one. 10.2.1: TRANSFER, slot KB entry, 10.3 rule 1, capped E3. NO `grade_tag`, following the seven prior_run entries already on disk, all of which carry none -- and that is a gap rather than a convention. 4.3.1 orders within E3 by grade_tag (peer_reviewed -> textbook -> vendor_spec -> preprint) and `prior_run` is not in that enum, so every prior-project item sorts last inside E3 by default rather than by anyone deciding it should. Against this store's own vendor_spec entries that ordering is arguably backwards here: this claim is an instrument verification of a vendor page, and it sorts below the page. }

  "claim": "On the prior project's bench the Lapp branch selector's enum names were false and its integer state was true: the configuration declared the label-to-position mapping inverted, so every label the device reported was the wrong name for the position it was in. The discipline that follows is to select that branch by integer and never by name.",
  "validity_conditions": "WHAT CROSSES IS THE DISCIPLINE, NOT THE LABEL, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE ENTRY. Their `mirror_in`/`mirror_out` strings and their State-to-position mapping are DOWNGRADE under 10.2.1 and are not entered: a label that was wrong there is not evidence here, and copying it would import the defect rather than the lesson. WHAT IT COST THEM: following the labels turned the light off, cost a diagnosis session, and the branch stood BOOKED AS FALSIFIED FOR TWO DAYS before the operator's own mapping showed the mislabelled enum was the fault. The record is worse than that: two further sites had been written by name and would have silently selected the BLOCKING position the moment the labels were corrected. Fixing the names would have broken the working config. Their repair was to convert every functional reference to the integer and to leave the `Label` lines in place only because the GUI needs names to show, with nothing selecting a position by one. WHY THIS MATTERS HERE RATHER THAN THERE: lapp_branch_assignment is open in this store and its own status already says it is settled by ACQUIRING and not by read-back. This entry supplies the reason that sentence is true -- this is the selector whose label and state read back consistently with each other for weeks while the mapping between them was inverted, so every signal a caller would normally trust agreed, and agreed wrongly. IT NARROWS lapp_branch_assignment AND DOES NOT CLOSE IT. The open question is which of widefield_source_a and widefield_source_b is which engine on THIS bench. Nothing here answers that: it is another bench's configuration defect, and 10.3 rule 1 caps it at E3 for exactly that reason. What it changes is what would count as an answer -- a label read back from this stand is not one, and a plan that pins the integer is not exposed to the mapping being wrong. That is a narrowing, and manager-microscope should read it as one. ONE DISCREPANCY IN THE RELAY, recorded rather than smoothed: task 029 quotes the source as saying `State 1 is the Aura position`. NO NUMBERS AND NO `validity`: this is a claim about how a device must be addressed, not a quantity, so a query's condition_range comes back unconstrained rather than satisfied. THIS IS THE FIGURE THAT SURVIVES IF THE CURVE IS EVER REMOVED, which is why it is entered separately from it and at a different grade and source. WHAT WOULD RAISE IT: measuring QE on this camera, which no axis has asked for. Slot: A1. Rules passed: 10.3 rule 1 for the cap, rule 2 for sourcing to the device document. `quantum_efficiency` was unregistered when this entry was written and the registration was raised rather than taken, because quantities.json is manager-librarian's; it landed the same day, defined as electrons per photon and therefore dimensionless, which is why the unit here is `1` and not something new.   "claim": "In its DynamicRange mode (16-bit) the Photometrics Kinetix22 has a read noise of 1.6 electrons rms, as specified by the datasheet's CAMERA MODES table. This is the widest dynamic range of the four and the datasheet's default choice when a bright object shares the frame with a dim one.",
  "numbers": [
    {
      "name": "read_noise",
      "value": 1.6,
      "unit": "e",
      "source": "spec:Kinetix22",
      "grade": "E3",
      "precision": "significant_figures",
      "note": "electrons rms, in the DynamicRange mode only. the unit is `e`, registered 2026-09-20 after this seat parked the value in `count` rather than inventing a symbol. The datasheet tabulates 1.6, 2.0, 1.2 and 0.7 across the four modes, a span of 2.9x, so a value quoted without its mode is not a fact about this camera."
    }
  ],
  "validity_conditions": "ONE MODE, AND THE ENTRY CANNOT BE READ FLATLY BECAUSE THERE IS NOTHING FLAT IN IT. The Kinetix22's read noise is a property of the selected camera mode, and the datasheet's CAMERA MODES table gives FOUR: DynamicRange 1.6, Speed 2.0, Sensitivity 1.2, SubElectron 0.7 electrons. They are filed as four entries for the reason the eight polystyrene wavelengths are eight: the datasheet could be wrong about one mode and right about the others, and a mode can be added or withdrawn by a firmware revision. A caller that does not name a mode gets four entries and no single answer, which is the correct refusal. THE TASK ASKED FOR THREE AND THERE ARE FOUR. 029 said three values and `M1/M2/M3`. Three is the mode count of the KINETIX, the 3200-row body, which the same file carries as a separate entry; the installed camera is the KINETIX22, confirmed 2026-08-19 as two bodies on PCIe and matched to the purchase record. The fourth mode is SubElectron at 0.7 electrons -- the lowest of all four, and the one an SNR-limited question would reach for first. Carrying three would have lost exactly the mode A1 most wants. THE UNIT IS `e` AND THE QUANTITY IS ELECTRONS RMS. It was `count` for the first hours of this entry's life, because the registry had no electron unit and 025's lesson is that an entry holding a unit a card would be refused for hands the defect to the first card that cites it. Registering `e`, and registering `read_noise`, were raised rather than taken -- both files are manager-librarian's -- and both landed the same day. `e` and `count` share dimension N and convert by exactly 1; what `e` carries is WHICH thing was counted. The registry's own note warns that ADU must never be given this dimension, because electrons and ADU differ by the camera's gain and sharing N would let the two convert silently. WHAT WOULD RAISE IT ABOVE E3: nothing about reading the sheet, which is still E3. Only measuring the read noise on this camera -- a dark series at the named mode -- makes it E1, and then this entry is superseded rather than edited (rule 8). NOT THE SAME NUMBER AS THE FLAT ONE THE PRIOR PROJECT KEPT. That file sets a single read_noise_e of 1.6 at the top of the block and warns in place that if a third consumer ever reads it flatly and computes, it must be made mode-aware instead. A1 computes SNR and is that third consumer, so this store is mode-aware from its first commit rather than flattened and fixed later. Slot: A1 `snr_floor`. Rules passed: 10.3 rule 1 for the E3 cap, rule 2 for sourcing to the device document.",
  "subject": [
    {
      "kind": "device",
      "id": "camera_red"
    }
  ],
  "source": "spec:Kinetix22",
  "grade": "E3",
  "grade_tag": "vendor_spec",
  "source_ref": "src_photometrics_kinetix22_datasheet_20241021",
  "identifiers": {
    "model": "Kinetix 22",
    "camera_mode": "DynamicRange",
    "bit_depth_designation": "16-bit"
  }
}

  "claim": "On the prior project's instrument the red particle's emission was strongest through emission wheel position 3, measured by running the same particle through all four single-band positions on 2026-09-06.",

  "source": "prior_run:agentic-microscope@filters-2026-09-06",

  "source_ref": "src_prior_filter_records",
  "validity_conditions": "MEASURED RATHER THAN CHOSEN, and the controls are what make it quantitative. The four positions gave 0.1, 1.6, 362.1 and 62.3 ADU. The first two bands sit blueward of the excitation and cannot carry fluorescence, so they read the floor at about 0.4 percent of the signal -- which is what establishes that the 677-701 band at 17.2 percent is real emission from the red tail of one broad emitter rather than bleed, and that position 3 wins by a real margin rather than a preference. The ADU figures themselves are NOT entered: instrument-specific, DISCARD under 10.2.1, and quoted here only as the reasoning behind the ranking. WHAT IT ESTABLISHES IS A BAND, NOT A PEAK, and the prior project says so itself: `Four bandpasses bracket a band, they do not locate a peak`, which is why it named a TRITC stand-in rather than inventing a number. A6 needs the wavelength actually collected and that is the band of position 3, not a peak inside it. CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY ON THIS BENCH. Today's E2 observation, particles_show_on_the_green_605_path, puts this bottle's emission in the same band on this instrument. Two observations, two instruments, two projects. The prior project's numbers are not borrowed for that -- the agreement is what makes borrowing unnecessary. WHICH WHEEL is not settled by this. emission_wheel_camera_mapping is E5 `operator_recall:` and says the first wheel serves red, `probably`. This entry is about positions WITHIN a wheel and neither confirms nor contradicts it. The store carries kelvin because the unit registry is multiplicative -- si_factor and a dimension vector cannot express an offset unit, so Celsius cannot enter it at all. 293 K rather than 293.15 K: the exact conversion would claim five figures from a reading given to the nearest degree, and the 0.15 K it drops is far inside the resolution of the reading."

  "validity_conditions": "The room as of 2026-09-17, operator read off a thermometer. CORRECTED 2026-09-19: this entry used to reason that the value could not be a setpoint because nothing actuates the temperature. That premise was false and the conclusion was right. The room IS held, by continuous air conditioning; what is not actuated is the SAMPLE, and the entry had collapsed the two. The grade never rested on that argument: 20 C is a value someone READ, which 12 grades differently from a setpoint, and a room value applied to the sample is not a measurement of the sample. A right answer standing on a wrong reason is the thing that rots, and as written the sentence asserted that this room is uncontrolled. The controlled room does not shrink the sample question, it ISOLATES it: with the room held, whatever still moves at the sample is local -- illumination, a contacting objective, the stage -- and those have their own open gap. Do not read 'the room is controlled' as 'temperature is handled'. WHERE the thermometer sits is now stated rather than inferred (no_thermometer_at_the_sample): it reads the room, and how far that is from the sample and how well the two track are both unknown. A plan needing the viscosity or the thermal energy AT THE SAMPLE stands on that gap rather than on this entry. Water's viscosity moves by roughly two percent per kelvin, so in explore mode a drift of about a kelvin does not move a decade and can be ignored, while in confirm mode it cannot. tracer_diffusivity_expected.text:
{
  "entry_id": "tracer_diffusivity_expected",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "derived_quantity",
  "claim": "The expected translational diffusivity of a tracer sphere in a bulk fluid is the Stokes-Einstein value, k_B T over 3 pi eta d. It is a prediction from the viscosity, the temperature and the diameter, not a measurement of how the particles actually move.",
  "symbol": "tracer_diffusivity_expected",
  "formula": "k_B*ambient_temperature/(3*pi*viscosity*tracer_diameter)",
  "inputs": [
    "ambient_temperature",
    "viscosity",
    "tracer_diameter"
  ],
  "unit": "um^2/s",
  "source": "computed:stokes_einstein",
  "grade": "E4",
  "grade_tag": "textbook",
  "source_ref": "src_colloid_dynamics",
  "validity_conditions": "A SPHERE IN BULK, WHICH IS WHERE THIS STOPS BEING TRUE FIRST. Stokes-Einstein assumes a rigid sphere, no slip at its surface, a continuum Newtonian fluid, dilute suspension so particles do not feel each other, and low Reynolds number. Near a wall the drag rises and the real diffusivity falls below this value -- the correction is applied separately and is NOT absorbed here, for the reason tau_d gives: fold it in and the quantity changes with stage position and nothing can be compared across runs. A tracer sitting on a coverslip is the case where this entry is most likely to be quietly wrong.\n\nWHY AN ENTRY RATHER THAN EACH CARD COMPUTING IT. plan.md:1295 ruled it: recomputing a quantity the store holds is not estimation, it is a detour. A simulation card cast tau_a = radius**2/D at E5 while kb:tau_d held diameter**2/D at E4 -- a factor of four out and a grade worse. A card citing this gets one name and the better grade; a card computing it gets neither. Filed as a formula rather than a value so that when an input improves the entry improves with it: the diameter went from an E5 recollection to an E2 measurement on 2026-09-19 and nothing here needs rewriting for that.\n\nTHE GRADE IS E4 AND THE CHECK DOES NOT DERIVE IT. 5.3 makes a `computed:` source max(E4, worst input). The worst input is E3 -- water_viscosity_293k E3, lab_ambient_temperature E3, tracer_diameter_measured E2 -- so E4. Check 43 does NOT confirm this: its `computed:` branch accepts E4 or E5 and never reads the inputs, so the number above is a reading of 5.3 by two people and not something the run established. Said out loud because 019 asked for the grade as the validator derives it, and the validator derives a range.\n\nTHE TEMPERATURE IS THE ROOM'S, NOT THE SAMPLE'S, AND THAT IS AN ASSUMPTION THIS ENTRY CARRIES. lab_ambient_temperature is a thermometer reading of the room; nothing actuates or reads the sample temperature (no_thermometer_at_the_sample, sample_temperature_not_actuated). declared_versus_inferred_temperature records why this is not symmetric between the two agents: the simulation DECLARES its temperature and realises it, so citing one there records a choice; the experiment INFERS it, so citing one there is a claim about the sample. This entry is on the inferring side. Under a trapping laser it is worse -- trap_heating_detection_bound bounds the heating only below about 20 per cent of the IR power and says nothing above it.\n\nUNITS: THE FORMULA IS SI AND THE DECLARED UNIT IS NOT. Evaluate with k_B in J/K, the temperature in K, the viscosity in Pa*s and the diameter in METRES, and the result is m^2/s. The entry declares um^2/s because that is the scale this store and both agents report diffusivity in -- quantities.json records the whole family at um^2/s -- and units.json's si_factor is what converts. Putting the diameter in um while the viscosity is in Pa*s and reading the answer as um^2/s is out by a factor of 10^6, which is six orders and would not look like a slip in a log.\n\nNOT `tracer_diffusivity`, AND NOT `diffusivity`. Three near-names now sit in one family and two of them are already in quantities.json's open_collisions. `tracer_diffusivity` is the REGISTERED OBSERVABLE: what an experiment measures and what the bridge threads between the two agents. `diffusivity` is the name the simulation writes, six uses, colliding with that observable. This one is the PREDICTION -- what Stokes-Einstein says the value should be given the inputs. The distinction is load-bearing rather than pedantic: the whole point of thr-tracer-diffusivity-001 is to compare a measured diffusivity against a modelled one, and an expected value quietly substituted for either side would make the comparison compare a prediction with itself. `_expected` is the word that keeps them apart and it has to survive any later rename.\n\nNO `subject`, AND THE REASON CHANGED ON 2026-09-20 WHILE THE ANSWER DID NOT. What this paragraph said until now: a quantity subject must resolve against check 44's registry -- the names used in numbers[] anywhere, united with those declared in contracts/quantities.json -- and `tracer_diffusivity_expected` was in neither, because this entry is a formula carrying no numbers[] and the two microscope axes that want it name it in `missing[]` and in a gap's `observable`, which the registry does not read. That was a BLOCK and it named manager-librarian as the route out. THE BLOCK IS GONE: the id is now declared in contracts/quantities.json, measured there on 2026-09-20 among sixteen, so a quantity subject would resolve today. Left off anyway, and now for a standing reason rather than a blocked one: `Store.subjects` is a UNION over entry_id, symbol, numbers[].name, subject[].id and the addressable identifiers, and both entry_id and symbol are already this exact string -- so a subject naming it would add no handle that is not already there. Measured and not reasoned: `answers_to` returns this entry for the bare name today, with the field absent. It stays empty because it would be a duplicate, not because anything is waiting on anybody. WRITTEN OUT RATHER THAN DELETED: a sentence saying a landed thing is still owed sends the next reader to raise it a second time, which is the failure this repository keeps recording, and deleting it instead would leave that reader to rediscover that a quantity subject is possible here and wonder why nobody filled it.\n\nITS INPUTS ARE FORMAL PARAMETERS TOO, AND FOR A WHILE THAT WAS HIDDEN BY A COINCIDENCE. Task 020 ruled that a derived_quantity whose inputs are formal parameters is complete and takes no grade from them -- 5.3's max(E4, worst input) is a rule about a computed VALUE, and a relation composes no numbers. That ruling was argued about tau_d and it applies here identically: this is the same kind, with the same `formula` key, and `ambient_temperature`, `viscosity` and `tracer_diameter` are the arguments of Stokes-Einstein, not references to particular entries. What made check 62 treat the two differently was that these three names HAPPEN to be carried as values in this store while tau_d's `bead_diameter` is the open_collisions synonym of `tracer_diameter` and is carried by nothing. So the grade it derived here was a coincidence of vocabulary, and editing one string inside the formula would have created or destroyed it -- which is option 2 of task 020, refused at the front door, arriving at the side. manager-librarian caught this in the seat that wrote the ruling and reported the derived count as 2. It is 1: the only real derivation in the store is working_distance_is_measured_to_the_coverslip, which is a `claim` whose inputs are genuinely two quantities. This entry's E4 comes from the relation being textbook and would stand in a store holding no diameters at all.",
  "date": "2026-09-20",
  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": [],
  "curated_by": "kyuhwan"
}

{
  "entry_id": "trap_heating_detection_bound",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "The operator recalls not noticing a temperature change in the sample unless the infrared trapping laser was driven above roughly 20 percent on its dial. This records where noticing stopped, by means that were not recorded.",
  "subject": [
    { "kind": "device", "id": "optical_tweezers" },
    { "kind": "configuration", "id": "trapping" },
    { "kind": "quantity", "id": "temperature" }
  ],
  "source": "operator_recall:kyuhwan_20260919",
  "grade": "E5",
  "grade_tag": "operator_recall",
  "source_ref": "src_operator_recall_20260919",
  "validity_conditions": "THIS IS NOT A LIMIT AND MAY NOT BE USED AS ONE. 'Keep it under 20 percent' is the sentence someone lifts out of an entry and uses to parameterise a laser, and three separate rules forbid that: safety limits live in a file a person writes and in deterministic code (P0, 2.1 rule 7), they do not transfer (10.3 rule 4), and the grade forbids it on its own -- an E5 may not parameterise an irreversible action without a person's individual approval, and raising laser power onto a sample is irreversible to the sample. Anyone needing a bound writes one in envelope/safety.json after confirming it physically. Three things this says less than it appears to. It is RECALLED, not read, which is why it is E5 while the neighbouring instrument facts are E3. It is a DETECTION BOUND and not a zero: 'did not notice' was measured by unrecorded means, and 'no heating below 20 percent' is a stronger claim than was made. And 20 PERCENT IS A DIAL READING, not a power: a percentage of an unstated maximum is not a quantity, and writing it into numbers[] would not make it one -- the same ruling that keeps a nominal magnification out of numbers[], wearing different clothes. It does not close the heating gap. A measured heating rate is still absent, and a gap that looks satisfied by an E5 recollection is a false absence running backwards. What it does is sharpen what to measure: sweep the dial with a thermometer that has a recorded position, and the bound becomes a curve.",

  "schema_version": "0.1",

  "claim": "The catalogue working distances for the objectives on this nosepiece are measured from the front element to the coverslip's lens-facing surface, not to the sample plane. This is inferred from two facts the store already holds; no document was read that says it.",
  "subject": [
    {

      "id": "nosepiece"
    }
  ],
  "inputs": ["working_distance", "coverslip_thickness"],
  "source": "computed:working_distance_versus_coverslip",
  "grade": "E4",
  "grade_tag": "computed",
  "source_ref": "src_store_derivation",
  "validity_conditions": "THE INFERENCE, AND IT IS AN INFERENCE. Three of the six objectives have a catalogue working distance SHORTER than the coverslip this laboratory mounts on: 60x Oil at 150 um (objective_mrd71670), 100x Oil at 130 um (objective_mrd71970), and 40x WI from 160 um (objective_mrd77400), against coverslip_thickness 170 um (coverslip_thickness_in_use, E3, operator_read). If the catalogue measured to the SAMPLE PLANE, then at focus the front element of those three would sit nearer the sample than the glass is thick -- inside the coverslip. It cannot. So the catalogue measures to the coverslip's lens-facing surface, and the distance from front element to sample is the working distance plus the coverslip thickness.\n\nRECORDED AS AN INFERENCE OR NOT AT ALL, which is how task 021 put it and why this is E4 rather than E3. Nothing was read. Two E3 facts and one impossibility give it, and 5.3 caps a consequence at E4 however good its inputs are. A later reading of the Nikon catalogue that states the convention outright would supersede this at E3; a measurement on this bench would do better still.\n\nWHAT IT IS NOT NEEDED FOR. Not for the focus ceiling. Task 021 recorded the person's correction of an over-built argument: a lens is at its working distance when it is in focus, by definition, so `do not pass the working distance` means `do not pass focus` whichever surface the catalogue measured from. The convention does not enter that rule and the ceiling did not wait on it.\n\nWHAT IT IS NEEDED FOR. Anything computing an absolute Z in stage coordinates from the coverslip geometry -- where the sample plane sits relative to a focused objective, how far a stage may travel before the element meets glass, and any conversion between a focus position and a depth in the sample. Those need the plus-170 and get it wrong silently without this.\n\nWHY THIS ONE DERIVES AND declared_versus_inferred_temperature DOES NOT. Both are conclusions this store reasoned to rather than read, and both are `computed:` at E4. The difference is what they rest on: this rests on two QUANTITIES the store carries as numbers, `working_distance` and `coverslip_thickness`, so `inputs` resolves and check 62 can verify the grade. That entry rests on CLAIMS carrying no numbers, so nothing composes. Same source kind, two different shapes -- which is the gap raised with manager-librarian under task 020.",
